title: Free audit terms: one call, one written read-out, one per company

reader.who: A small business owner in Dhaka or London who has never met us, reading on a phone, maybe in a second language.
reader.decides: Whether to apply for the free audit, knowing exactly what they get, what they agree to, and that they owe nothing.
lacks: That the free audit is exactly one video call of up to 60 minutes and one written read-out, and that we do none of the work the read-out suggests.
That the 10 places go strictly in the order complete applications arrive, and that being on the waiting list does not promise a place.
That they owe nothing and are under no obligation to buy, and that nothing renews or charges automatically.

register_notes: Measured professional in form and child-clear in meaning: complete sentences, short paragraphs, and everyday words that a reader on a phone, perhaps in a second language, can follow in one pass. The tone is a calm host explaining the house rules, never a guard reading out penalties: each clause says plainly what happens, without threat, apology or legal wording. Write as "we" speaking to "you", and say every legal idea in the everyday words for it. No selling, no slogans, no jokes, and no em dashes.

glossary.the free audit: One video call of up to 60 minutes and one written read-out, given free; also "the audit", never a consultation, review or session.
glossary.the call: The one video call of up to 60 minutes that is part of the audit.
glossary.read-out: The one written document we send by email within 10 working days after the call; always "read-out", never report, letter or summary.
glossary.place: One of the 10 free audits on offer.
glossary.the waiting list: The queue of complete applications, kept strictly in the order they arrive by date and time; "the list" means the same thing.
glossary.complete application: The form filled in, with contact details that work.
glossary.working days: Sunday to Thursday, not counting public holidays in Bangladesh.
glossary.the offer: The free audit offer as a whole, which runs for a limited time with no fixed end date.
glossary.paid work: Any work done for money later, under a new and separate agreement with its own written scope and terms.
glossary.paid client: A company with a separate paid agreement with us; never call someone taking the free audit a client.
glossary.competing studio or consultancy: Another studio or consultancy in competition with FlowState Impact.
glossary.we, us, our: FlowState Impact and the people who work in the studio.
glossary.you, your: The company taking the audit and the person who applies for it.
glossary.the studio: The people of FlowState Impact, as in "outside the studio" and "anyone in the studio".
glossary.these terms: The rules on this page, which together with the booking confirmation are the whole agreement for the audit.

never: Never mention Akij in any form.
Never say or hint that the studio chooses, judges or ranks who gets a place: no shortlisting, curating, selecting, "successful applicants", "chosen" or "accepted". Places go in order.
Never describe the legal form of the business (no sole trader, limited company or partnership), and never give a registration number or a street address.
Never claim an office, team or legal presence in London; the facts say only that the business is registered in Dhaka, Bangladesh.
Never add a number, date, price, promise, deadline or party that is not in the facts: no end date for the offer, no reply time for questions, no price or discount for paid work.
Never describe what the audit looks at beyond "your business"; the facts do not say.
Never use legal wording: hereinafter, shall, notwithstanding, the Client, whereas, herein, thereof, force majeure, or any legal Latin.

Never use a word on the studio ban list, including: certainly, of course, absolutely, leverage, seamless, journey, unlock, empower, elevate, solution, robust, innovative, cutting-edge, framework, ecosystem, synergy, passionate, worth, ultimately, in conclusion, to summarize.
Never use an em dash; use a full stop or a comma instead.
Never sell, joke or write a slogan, and never praise the studio or the value of the audit.
Never sound like a guard reading out penalties: no threats, no "failure to comply", no "prohibited"; say calmly what happens.
Never merge two clauses under one heading, never drop a clause, and never change the order of groups A to J or of the clauses inside them.
Never renumber or drop the clause numbers 1 to 39; each clause keeps its number before its heading, because clause 34 points back to clauses 5, 17, 24 and 26.

Never give a clause a bare label heading (Eligibility, Intellectual Property, Liability, Termination, Governing Law, Severability); every clause heading states its point, like "You keep your read-out".
Never write a paragraph in capital letters; only THE SHORT VERSION and the group headings keep the capitals the brief gives them.
Never call the read-out a report, letter or summary, or the audit a consultation; use the glossary terms.
Never promise that being on the waiting list leads to a place.
Never change the company name from FlowState Impact.
Never fill in CONTACT_EMAIL or LAST_UPDATED; write both tokens exactly as they are.
Never close a section with a summary, a recap or a sign-off.

sections.heading: You get one free call and one written read-out, and each company takes part once
sections.purpose: The reader can say back the whole deal from THE SHORT VERSION (one free call, one written read-out, waiting-list order, one per company, no obligation), then knows from group A who may apply and that each company takes part only once.
facts: Company: FlowState Impact, a business registered in Dhaka, Bangladesh.
Open with THE SHORT VERSION: four or five plain sentences (one free call, one written read-out, waiting-list order, one per company, no obligation).
The audit is one video call of up to 60 minutes and one written read-out, sent by email within 10 working days after the call.
There are 10 places. Places go strictly in the order complete applications arrive, by the date and time we receive them.
You owe us nothing and are under no obligation to buy anything.

Then the full terms in ten groups, A to J, in the order below. Each clause gets its own short plain heading that states its point (for example "You keep your read-out", never "Intellectual Property"), followed by one to three sentences. Keep the clause order.
A. WHO CAN TAKE PART
1. One free audit per company, once.
2. Companies with the same owner, the same group or the same management count as one company.
3. A company that has had its audit, or lost its place under these terms, cannot apply again under another name, a new trading name or through another person.
4. The person applying must be the owner, a director, or someone the owner has allowed to apply and to share business details.
5. People who run or work for a competing studio or consultancy cannot take part, including applying for them or for their clients. If this comes to light later, the audit ends.
sections.carry_in: Nothing yet: the reader has tapped the star beside "Free for a limited time" on an audit button and knows only that the audit is free.
sections.hand_off: Section 2 shows how the 10 places are handed out in order and exactly what one place gives and does not give.

sections.heading: The 10 places go in the order applications arrive, and a place gives you one call and one read-out
sections.purpose: The reader understands that the 10 places go strictly by arrival time and cannot be traded, what happens when they are full or the offer closes, and exactly where the free audit stops and paid work would begin.
facts: Each clause gets its own short plain heading that states its point (for example "You keep your read-out", never "Intellectual Property"), followed by one to three sentences. Keep the clause order.
B. THE WAITING LIST
6. There are 10 places. Places go strictly in the order complete applications arrive, by the date and time we receive them.
7. An application is complete when the form is filled in and the contact details work. We confirm a place on the list by email within 2 working days.
8. A place belongs to the company and cannot be sold, swapped, handed to another business, or exchanged for money, a discount or any paid alternative.
9. When the 10 places are filled, new applicants stay on the waiting list, in order. If a place frees up, it goes to the next on the list. Being on the list does not promise a place.

10. The offer runs for a limited time. There is no fixed end date. It ends when the 10 places are used, or earlier if we close it; if we close it, we say so on this page and tell everyone still on the list by email. A place on the list does not carry over to any later offer unless we say so in writing.
C. WHAT YOU GET, AND WHAT YOU DO NOT
11. The audit is one video call of up to 60 minutes and one written read-out, sent by email within 10 working days after the call.
12. Working days are Sunday to Thursday, not counting public holidays in Bangladesh. If something outside our control delays the read-out, we say so and give a new date.

13. We do not carry out any of the work the read-out suggests: no design, writing, building, strategy work, extra calls, unlimited follow-up questions or rewriting of the read-out. You may send one email of questions about the read-out within 14 days of receiving it, and we answer it once.
14. The read-out is a finished document, not a draft. We do not rewrite it to match a view you prefer. If we got a fact wrong through our own mistake, tell us and we correct that fact.
15. Paid work, if you want it later, is a new and separate agreement with its own written scope and terms. Nothing in the read-out is a price, a quote or a promise of what paid work would include.
sections.carry_in: The reader knows the deal in a few sentences and who may apply, once per company.
sections.hand_off: Section 3 sets out what the reader gives in return: true details, a kept call, and respect for who owns what.

sections.heading: Your part is true details, a kept call, and respect for what each side owns
sections.purpose: The reader understands that the read-out is only as good as what they share, what happens if the call is moved, missed or joined late, and that they keep their read-out for their own use while our methods stay ours and nobody records the call without both sides agreeing.
facts: Each clause gets its own short plain heading that states its point (for example "You keep your read-out", never "Intellectual Property"), followed by one to three sentences. Keep the clause order.
D. WHAT WE NEED FROM YOU

16. The read-out rests on what you share. We may send a short set of questions before the call. If the information is incomplete or wrong, the read-out will be too, and we are not responsible for that.
17. Giving false details ends the audit: a false company name, a false role, or hiding that you work for a competing studio.
E. MOVED, MISSED OR LATE CALLS
18. To move the call, tell us at least 24 hours before. You can move it once. After that, the place goes to the next on the list.
19. If you do not join and did not tell us, we wait 15 minutes, then the call is closed and the place passes to the next on the list.
20. If you join late, the call still ends at its booked time.
21. If we need to move the call, we tell you as early as we can and offer a new time. You keep your place.
F. WHO OWNS WHAT
22. You keep the read-out for your own business use. You may share it inside your company and with your own advisers, for example your accountant or lawyer.
23. Our questions, the way we structure the read-out, our templates, scoring and working tools stay the property of FlowState Impact. Receiving a read-out gives no right to them.
24. The read-out may not be sold, posted publicly, used to train software, presented as your own work, or used to give the same service to others.
25. Using our name, the read-out or quotes from it in marketing or the press needs our written permission first.
26. No recording or sharing of the call unless both sides agree first. This includes AI note-taking tools and meeting bots. We take our own written notes.
sections.carry_in: The reader knows places go in arrival order and that a place is one call and one read-out, with no extra work.
sections.hand_off: Section 4 closes the terms: the limits of the advice, no obligation either way, privacy, when an audit can end, and where to send a question.

sections.heading: You owe us nothing, your details stay private, and any ending or change is told to you
sections.purpose: The reader understands the limits of the advice, that neither side owes the other anything more, how their details are kept and deleted, when an audit or the offer can end and how they are told, and that their next step with any question about these terms is to write to the contact address.
facts: Each clause gets its own short plain heading that states its point (for example "You keep your read-out", never "Intellectual Property"), followed by one to three sentences. Keep the clause order.
G. ADVICE, RESPONSIBILITY AND NO OBLIGATION
27. The audit is not legal, financial, tax or accounting advice. For those, speak to a qualified professional.

28. The read-out is our honest view on the day it is written. We promise no result from following it, and we are not responsible for decisions you make or losses that follow, as far as the law allows. Nothing here removes rights that the law says cannot be removed.

29. You owe us nothing and are under no obligation to buy anything. We are under no obligation to offer paid work. We may tell you once what paid work would look like; we will not chase you, and nothing renews or charges automatically.
H. PRIVACY

30. What you share is used only to prepare your audit. We do not share it outside the studio, except where the law requires it, or with a trusted contractor who works for us under the same duty of privacy.

31. If we want to use a lesson from your audit with your name and details removed, for example in an article, we ask you first in writing. Using your name or company in a case study needs a separate written yes.
32. We keep audit material for 12 months, then delete it, unless you become a paid client. Data protection rights you have where you live still apply.
33. We do not add you to a mailing list unless you say yes.
I. WHEN WE MAY DECLINE, PAUSE OR END AN AUDIT

34. We may decline, pause or end an audit when a rule here is broken: false details (17), working for or applying for a competing studio (5), recording or sharing without agreement (26), resale or misuse of the read-out (24), or rude, threatening or abusive behaviour towards anyone in the studio. When we do, we tell you which rule was broken.
35. If running your audit would mean using what another client told us in private, we tell you and cannot run it. You keep your place on the list if the conflict ends while the offer is open.
J. GENERAL

36. We may change or end the offer. Changes are posted on this page with the date. A change never takes away a place already confirmed, or the call and read-out already promised to someone holding one.
37. These terms and your booking confirmation are the whole agreement for the audit. If one clause turns out not to be valid, the rest still stand.
38. These terms follow the law of Bangladesh, and the courts of Dhaka decide any dispute. Before going to court, both sides first try to settle a problem in writing for 30 days.
39. Contact: questions about these terms go to CONTACT_EMAIL. Last updated: LAST_UPDATED. (Write the two capitalised tokens exactly as they are; they are filled in by hand later.)
sections.carry_in: The reader knows what they get, how places are given, and what they must do and respect during the audit.
sections.hand_off: Nothing follows; the page ends on the contact line and the last-updated date.

gaps: What the audit looks at (brand, website, marketing, operations or something else): until this is given, the page can only say "about your business".
How someone applies from this page: the link or wording that points to the application form.
How and when the call time is agreed once a place comes up, and who picks it.
Whether the email in clause 7 confirms one of the 10 places or only a position on the waiting list; clause 36 protects "a place already confirmed", so the difference matters.
Whether the "booking confirmation" in clause 37 is the same email as the clause 7 confirmation or a separate one.
What counts as a "competing studio or consultancy" in clauses 5, 17 and 34: branding and design studios only, or any consultancy.
Whether companies outside Bangladesh and the UK may apply.
Which language the call and the read-out are in, and which time zone call times are given in for a London business.
How soon we answer the one email of questions allowed in clause 13.
Whether the page spells the name FlowState Impact, as the brief does, or with the tilde the studio uses elsewhere.
